title: Studying music: Hammond and Gerlach, Gene Jenkins teaches harmony
summary: He began to study seriously at a Penn Avenue music store school and learned chords and harmony at the piano from Gene Jenkins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, now you had to start to read music.
Yeah, I really had to start then.
Well, how did --
I started seriously.
Well, did you study or --

Yeah, I was studying with Hammond and Gerlach (PHONETIC). It was two partners who had a big music store on Penn Avenue, in Pittsburgh, and they had a music school in the store, upstairs. Like they sold instruments downstairs and upstairs they had a school.
Oh.
So I used to deliver things for them and finally --
Yeah.
You know, I worked my way into studying a little bit with them.
Oh, that was terrific. Well, that must be a real thrill for you to start working out changes and all that.
Oh, yeah, yeah. Well, the saxophone player we worked with when I took the job from Biddie Johnson gave me the job in the cabaret, he started teaching me harmony.
He did.
And I learned harmony from him.
Well, how did you learn harmony, on the piano?
Yeah, on the piano. He was a wonderful musician.
Do you play some piano now?
Yeah, I can play. I compose a lot, you know.
Do you really.
I learned it all from -- mostly from Gene, Gene Jenkins.
Fancy that.
He taught me. He said, 'Come on, kid.
I'm going to teach you all your chords. Now, you have to know your chords." And it was good of him to teach you. That -- because you were a drummer.
That's right. He just figured I should know that.
Yeah.

So he would teach me like C, now this is the 7th, this is the 6th, this is the 13th, this is the 9th. And I started out. Now we go to C-sharp, and this is so and so and this is so and so, and all the way. He taught me the whole thing, the whole bit.
Isn't that wonderful.
